paper.title: Temperature dependence of the deformation behavior and mechanical properties of a Fe–Mn–Al–C low-density steel for cryogenic application
paper.journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
paper.paper_scope: Studies the temperature dependence of the deformation behavior and mechanical properties of a single Fe-20Mn-6Al-0.6C-0.15Si austenitic low-density steel by tensile and Charpy impact tests at -196°C, -77°C and room temperature, correlating reduced SFE and promoted planar glide with tensile properties and cryogenic impact toughness.

alloys.description: Single experimental alloy studied throughout the paper; a fully austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steel melted and cast in a 50 kg vacuum induction furnace for cryogenic-application research.
alloys.alloys_notes: Estimated density by Kim et al. equation is 7.078 g/cm3; measured density is 7.114 g/cm3. Initial microstructure is fully austenitic (equiaxed grains) with no isothermal martensite at -196°C.

unmapped_findings: Calculated SFE of the experimental steel is 32, 40 and 61 mJ/m2 at -196°C, -77°C and RT, respectively (block b0050).
Charpy impact absorbed energy Wall is about 327 J at RT, 277 J at -77°C and 188 J at -196°C (block b0037).
Crack initiation energy Winitiation is 112, 68 and 57 J at -196°C, -77°C and RT, respectively (block b0072).
Measured density of the steel is 7.114 g/cm3 versus estimated 7.078 g/cm3 (block b0026).

At -196°C a small amount of mechanical twins forms during tensile deformation; at -77°C no twins but microbands are observed; secondary cracks are present near the fracture after RT impact test (blocks b0033, b0035, b0073).
